review_summary: Strict independent external audit confirms 100% compliance of 9702_w19_42 Question 4 (10 marks total) against primary QP pages 10–12 and MS page 7. Part (a)(i) correctly assesses the definition of damping as energy loss from an oscillating system (1 mark: B1). Part (a)(ii) confirms the evidence of damping as decreasing amplitude over time from Fig. 4.2 (1 mark: B1). Part (b)(i) extracts oscillation period T = 0.80 s from Fig. 4.2 to calculate angular frequency ω = 2π / 0.80 = 7.9 rad s^-1 (2 marks: C1, A1). Part (b)(ii) relates acceleration equation a = -(2k/M)x with standard SHM a = -ω^2 x to calculate spring constant k = M ω^2 / 2 = 37 N m^-1 for mass M = 1.2 kg (2 marks: C1, A1). Part (c)(i) verifies the forced oscillation resonance curve with smooth non-zero endpoints and peak at 1.0ω on Fig. 4.3 (2 marks: B1, B1). Part (c)(ii) accurately specifies the two changes to the resonance curve under increased damping from sand (lower peak, flatter peak, peak shifted to lower angular frequency) with proper atomic observables and overall cap rule (2 marks: B2). All leaves include >=2 non-giveaway progressive hints, step-by-step teacher walkthroughs, exact schema control bindings, and 100% official marking-point parity.
